name: No web frontend
summary: Nothing is shown in a browser: an API, or the backend of a mobile app.

name: Static site
summary: Pages are built ahead of time and served as files.

learning-curve.why: Mostly HTML and CSS; little to set up

performance.why: Consistently fast first byte and first paint; little JavaScript to run

sources.note: static rendering: fast TTFB and FCP, low TBT/INP

seo.why: Every page arrives as complete HTML, so search engines read it directly

sources.note: complete HTML, as with server rendering
Astro and Next.js static export docs

interactivity.why: Interactive parts need extra JavaScript on top of the pages

sources.note: static rendering: progressive enhancement, limited client JS

cost.why: Files on a CDN; free static hosting exists

sources.note: can be served from many CDNs
GitHub Pages hosts static HTML, CSS and JS files for free

name: Single-page app (SPA)
summary: The browser builds the pages with JavaScript.

learning-curve.why: A component framework, state and client-side routing to learn

performance.why: First paint waits for JavaScript; hard to keep fast on phones as the app grows

sources.note: client-side rendering: difficult to make and keep fast on mobile

seo.why: Crawlers can run JavaScript but with limits; needs extra testing

sources.note: CSR can work for SEO but needs extra testing and overhead

interactivity.why: Built for app-like behaviour: everything happens in the browser

cost.why: Builds to static files that any static host can serve

sources.note: GitHub Pages hosts static HTML, CSS and JS files for free

name: Server-rendered (meta-framework)
summary: A framework renders pages on the server, then makes them interactive in the browser.

learning-curve.why: Component framework plus server/client split, data loading and caching rules

performance.why: Fast first paint, but hydration ships the app twice and delays input

sources.note: SSR: fast FCP; hydration: TBT/INP cost, 'one app for the price of two'
SSR delivers a complete-looking page crawlers can read

cost.why: Needs a server or functions to render pages; highest server cost of the approaches

name: Pages from the backend
summary: The backend framework renders HTML templates (Blade, Django templates, Thymeleaf, Razor).

learning-curve.why: Templates in the language the team already uses; no second app

performance.why: Server-rendered HTML without hydration; little JavaScript

sources.note: SSR without rehydration: fast FCP, low TBT; TTFB cost
Django, Laravel, Spring, ASP.NET Core template docs

interactivity.why: Each action usually loads a new page; rich widgets need extra JavaScript

sources.note: plain SSR suits content and links

cost.why: Rendered by the backend you already run; no extra server

name: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript
summary: Hand-written pages with no framework or build step.

sources.note: open web standards, nothing to install

learning-curve.why: HTML and CSS are the first core modules of MDN's curriculum; frameworks come later, after JavaScript

sources.note: MDN Learn web development: core modules start with structuring content (HTML) and styling (CSS); frameworks are an extension module

productivity.why: No components or build tools; repeated markup is copied by hand

performance.why: Ships only the HTML, CSS and JavaScript you write (rendering band 5); no CWV category exists for 'no framework'

sources.note: static rendering: 'fine to mostly ship HTML with minimal JavaScript'

ecosystem.why: Any library can be added by hand, but nothing is integrated

sources.note: 2026 languages, HTML/CSS, all respondents, official data StackExchange/Survey technology.json; `npm run sources`

maturity.why: HTML is a living standard maintained by browser makers since 2004, backwards-compatible

type-safety.why: No type checking unless you add TypeScript or JSDoc checks yourself

name: No database
summary: Nothing is stored, so no database is needed.

name: Relational (SQL)
summary: Tables with relationships, queried with SQL.

learning-curve.why: SQL and schema design take some learning

performance.why: Fast for typical lookups and joins with indexes

scalability.why: Usually scales up one machine first; scaling out needs extra work

real-time.why: Some products can push changes (e.g. PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY)

data-integrity.why: Multi-record transactions and constraints are central to the model

schema-flexibility.why: Schema-on-write, but JSON columns allow varying fields

name: Document
summary: Self-contained documents (JSON-like) loaded as a whole.

learning-curve.why: Documents look like the objects in your code

performance.why: A whole document is read in one go (locality)

scalability.why: Built-in sharding is common in this category

data-integrity.why: One document is updated atomically; no foreign keys in the model

schema-flexibility.why: Schema-on-read: items can have different fields

name: Key-value
summary: Values looked up by a key, often kept in memory.

learning-curve.why: Few concepts: get and set by key

performance.why: In-memory stores answer lookups very fast

scalability.why: Keys spread easily across machines

real-time.why: Many key-value stores have publish/subscribe (Unsourced: held at 3 until a non-GK source is found.)

data-integrity.why: In-memory stores with asynchronous disk writes can lose recent writes on a crash

schema-flexibility.why: Values are opaque; structure is up to the app

coverageExempt.reason: Mainly a secondary store: no v1 app kind is one where a neutral senior developer keeps all the app's data in a key-value store (recent writes can be lost on a crash, no queries beyond the key). Its honest uses (cache, sessions, rate limits, queues, pub/sub) sit next to a main database. Rule D7 still lets it win for 'only simple lookups'.

name: Graph
summary: Nodes and relationships, for highly connected data.

learning-curve.why: Needs a new query language such as Cypher

performance.why: Fast at following relationships, average otherwise

scalability.why: Hard to split a connected graph across machines

schema-flexibility.why: Easy to add new kinds of nodes and relationships

name: PostgreSQL
summary: Open-source relational database with strong SQL, transactions and JSON support.

learning-curve.why: Standard SQL; many features to learn over time

performance.why: Fast for typical web workloads with indexes

scalability.why: Replication built in; scaling writes out needs extensions or sharding tools

real-time.why: LISTEN/NOTIFY and logical replication can push changes

data-integrity.why: Full transactions and constraints; detects lost updates at repeatable read

ecosystem.why: Drivers and ORMs for every major language; many managed hosts (Unsourced: held at 3 until a non-GK source is found.)
